Author: M.Laxman
Bench: M.Laxman
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice M.Laxman
 Criminal Petition No.4325 of 2021
Order:

1. The present Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short 'Cr.P.C') by the petitioner/accused No.5 seeking to quash the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.638 of 2017 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad,
arising out of Crime No.768 of 2015 of Women Police Station, Detective Department, Hyderabad,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 406, 420, 506 and 354 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The petitioner herein is accused No.5 and respondent No.2 herein is victim/de facto complainant.
2. The case of the prosecution is that the marriage of the victim was performed with accused No.1 and at the time of marriage, some gold and dowry amounts were given to the accused.
The present petitioner/accused No.5 is sister of accused No.1 and sister-in-law of victim, who resides in United States of America (USA).
After marriage, victim stayed in her in-laws house for a period of six months, where she was subjected to harassment by the accused.
Subsequently, she went to Canada to reside with accused No.1, but from the airport at Canada, accused No.1 took the victim to USA to the house of accused No.5 and they stayed there for three days.
At that time, the victim kept her gold with accused No.5, which she did not return to the victim.
Apart from these, there are several other allegations made by the victim against other accused, for the purpose of the present proceedings they are not considered.
The only allegation made against the present petitioner/accused No.5 by the victim is that she kept her gold with accused No.5 and she misappropriated the same.

3. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.5 that no such gold was kept with accused No.5 and such a claim of the victim was also disbelieved by the Family Court in the O.P filed for dissolution of marriage and findings of the Civil Court in said proceedings were not challenged by the victim.
Therefore, according to him, except said allegation of gold being kept with accused No.5, no other allegations attract the offences charged in the charge sheet against accused No.5.
Therefore, he prayed to quash the criminal proceedings.

4. It is the contention of the learned counsel for respondent No.2/victim that the allegations in statement and complaint of the victim clearly shows that accused No.5 played a key role in the marriage of victim and accused No.1.
It is also contended that the there are allegations that after victim reached Canada, she was taken to the house of accused No.5 in USA and they stayed together for three days.

During her stay in USA, the gold of the victim was kept with accused No.5 and such Meghana Maheshwaram vs The State Of Telangana on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82215643/
1 gold was not returned to her.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for victim contended that when such is the allegation,
this Court cannot quash criminal proceedings against accused No.5.
5.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed quashment of criminal proceedings against accused No.5.
6.
There is no doubt that there is allegation that gold was kept with accused No.5.

It is also not in dispute that there are findings from the Civil Court where the claim of the victim that gold was kept with present petitioner i.e., accused No.5 was disbelieved and such findings have attained finality, as no challenge was made to such findings.
The said judgment in the case of dissolution of marriage is unimpeachable and sterling in character.
Therefore, such findings have some bearing on the present petitioner while considering the allegations relating to entrustment of gold to accused No.5 by the victim.
In the said circumstances, this Court feels that continuation of criminal proceedings against accused No.5 is clear abuse of process of law and the same are liable to be quashed.

7. In the result, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.638 of 2017 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad, arising out of Crime No.768 of 2015 of Women Police Station, Detective Department, Hyderabad, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 406, 420, 506 and 354 of the Indian Penal Code, 1870 and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, against the present petitioner i.e., accused No.5 are hereby quashed and she is acquitted for the above said offences.
